expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: The list goes "**Peer-reviewed research**" (#1–3), then "**Preprints and working papers**" (#4–6), then "**Survey reports**" (#7–8).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Each preprint (#4–6) has a "*Watch for:*" note, and #4 and #5 also have "*Why it's here:*". The survey group's heading explains it: "they show how common chatbot use is, not whether it helps or hurts learning".

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "I checked the journal for all three in Crossref, so these count toward your 3 peer-reviewed"

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: The reply shows no scores, tiers or named rating levels. Sources are only grouped by type, such as "Peer-reviewed article" and "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed."

expectations.text: Every link or DOI in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: The tool log shows a WebFetch for every link in the reply: ideas.repec.org, chibe.upenn.edu, arxiv 2412.09315, arxiv 2409.09047, arxiv 2605.21629 and both Pew pages. The reply gives no DOI links.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: The only question mark aimed at the user is in "Which source surprised you most?". The items under "Questions the results raise" have no question marks.
